## Example 4.7 {#ss4-example-4-7 .ar-lesson .ar-cans-slide}

A supermarket displays cans of fruit in the form of a ‘pyramid’. There are $5$ cans in the top row, $7$ in the next, $9$ in the one after that and so on. Given there are $15$ rows on display, find:

::: {.split .ar-cans-layout}
::: {.column-block}
a\) the number of cans in the bottom row;

b\) the total number of cans in the display.

::: {.takeaway .fragment data-fragment-index="0"}
One row gives a term.<br>The whole display gives a sum.

:::

:::
::: {.column-block}
<img class="ar-cans-diagram" src="../media/arithmetic-can-display.svg" alt="Fifteen centred rows of cans, starting with 5, then 7, then 9, and increasing by 2 per row. The first four rows are labelled with their row number and 5, 7, 9 and 11 cans. The bottom row is highlighted.">

:::

:::

<p class="booklet-cue">Booklet p. 24 · Example 4.7</p>

::: notes

The exact diagram contains 15 rows with 5+2(r−1) cans in row r, a total of 285. The bottom row is highlighted to connect with part (a), while the full diagram relates to part (b). a=5,d=2,n=15. Bottom row a_15=5+14(2)=33. Total S_15=15(5+33)/2=285. Do not count the bottom row as the total. Reveal the term/sum distinction after students identify which formula each part requires.

:::
